message: Can you read this ECG for me?
reply:
**This ECG is abnormal and is concerning for a type 1 Brugada pattern.** A clinician should review the original tracing promptly.

My reading from the image:

- **Sinus rhythm**, roughly **70 beats/min**, with some variation in the time between beats.
- Marked **ST elevation followed by inverted T waves in V1–V3**, extending into V4.
- The shape of these changes resembles the “coved” pattern associated with Brugada. [ESC description](https://www.escardio.org/communities/councils/cardiology-practice/scientific-documents-and-publications/ejournal/volume-19/brugada-syndrome-and-sports-activity-from-history-to-risk-stratification/)

This image alone cannot establish **Brugada syndrome**. Lead placement, medications, electrolyte disturbances and other heart conditions can produce similar appearances. Confirming the finding matters because Brugada syndrome can increase the risk of dangerous heart rhythms. [Clinical overview](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK1517/)

**If you currently have chest pain, fainting, severe dizziness, or palpitations with feeling unwell, seek emergency care now and do not drive yourself.** If you feel well and this is a new finding, arrange prompt cardiology review, ideally with a heart rhythm specialist.

Was this ECG taken because of symptoms, and have you ever fainted or had a family member die suddenly at a young age?
